description: This team is made up with students from the middle school IMANTI located in Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico
summary: Our project educates about the numerous risks and hazards that could hypothetically happen on a mission on Mars. Utilizing the recent discovery of biosignatures present in the Jezero Crater, we created an interactive game for kids to solve issues that could happen during the investigation. Using the abundant amount of resources provided by NASA, our team constructed a decision based web browser game. Our game not only addresses the difficulty and hardship that astronauts face during a mission, but it also was created to enlighten our community, and still give the liberty of imagination while playing. Our game yields a lot of significance to teaching scientific occurrences and phenomena to younger people, and addresses the curiosity of what would happen if astronauts went to Mars.
details:
Our project is to enlighten people in a fun interactive way about the difficulties and hazards of space missions, and the success rates of a mission to Mars. Our team made a series of scenes and events where decisions are needed to be taken, hence every action affects all the parameters needed to succeed a mission and deplete them accordingly within the game. Our team used the coding languages HTML, CSS, and Javascript. And was implemented as a decisive web browser game. Our game provides different endings according to what decisions you have chosen. We have also considered the many risks of residing in a settlement on Mars, from Gamma Ray Bursts to dust storms. We purposefully added those situations for the benefit of figuring out the best course of action that the younger community has to decide while playing the game, as well as impacting the younger community in learning how a mission to Mars can be overwhelming. We also have added some imagination to the mission by giving curiosity via a prior mission regarding biosignatures present on Mars. We designed some of the components ourselves, such as the drawings and ideas. Our team also utilized the aid of Google Gemini to generate the initial code and debug errors. Then we published it using Github Pages.

How the game works:

Our game is a decisive web browser game, it initializes by telling the user they have successfully touched down in the Isidis Planitia region, which we chose using Mars Trek to imagine where an outpost investigating the Jezero Crater would be. In the first part of the game you receive a random event or phenomena out of six that each of our team members have created. You receive the event or phenomena and you have to decide which systems out of two that are chosen from Life Support, Radiation Shielding, Energy and Aliments that you decide to save. Once you decide, it depletes or augments the systems accordingly. Your objective is to have enough of each system to succeed the mission. On every event or phenomena description, there is a picture regarding it or of Mars provided by APOD (Astronomy Picture Of the Day). After your first two events, you will encounter the decision of either: Continuing the main mission or risk it and do a sidequest.  After you decide, the game will tell you what your main mission is, and to decide what to do based on the situation. Some of those decisions that you have selected can lead you into a mini game we created, that is interactive and a fun break in the game. During the course of the game, as well as your systems being augmented or diminished, you also gain points of discovery, which decides if your mission was a success in discovering the ancient remnants of microbes in the Jezero Crater. The mini game gives you additional discovery points to succeed the mission. At the end of the game you have three alternative endings. The first is Mission Accomplished, which means that you have successfully discovered something during your mission and have enough from each of the systems to survive. The second ending,  Mission Complete, means that you have survived and have all the systems but you haven’t discovered anything during your mission. And last, Mission Failure means you do not have enough in the systems to survive without a rescue and haven’t discovered anything.
